analysis.title: Equities - Tactical Top Picks
key_insights: UBS Unified Global Markets PMA Equity Sales published its Tactical Top Picks list on 6 Nov 2026 with 9 open ideas: Straumann (STMN SW, new), Rolls-Royce, Siemens, Barclays, ROCKWOOL, Oracle, Boeing, Expeditors and Orica. All are rated Buy, and 6 of the 9 (all except Straumann, ROCKWOOL and Expeditors) carry the CIO Most Preferred (MP) tag.
Open ideas performance since inception to 6 Nov 2026: Straumann +13.8%, Rolls-Royce -6.9%, Siemens -0.9%, Barclays -11.4%, ROCKWOOL +0.5%, Oracle -3.4%, Boeing -10.5%, Expeditors +0.3%, Orica -1.5%.

Closed ideas year-to-date 2026: 80 ideas, average absolute performance -0.4% and average relative performance -1.6%, annualized alpha -12.7%. Switzerland +6.8% absolute / +3.4% relative, Europe -0.4% / -1.6%, Americas -0.7% / -2.0%, Asia-Pacific -6.2% / -4.1%.

Since-inception track record of closed ideas: 273 ideas, average absolute performance +1.2% and relative +0.2%, with an average life of 38 trading days. By year, the average absolute return was 3.6% in 2026 YTD for one region cohort and 2.0%/1.7% in others, but the overall record is close to benchmark.

Straumann (Buy, PT CHF 115): UBS sees consensus forecasts as achievable with modest scope for earnings outperformance. Dental implants are among the fastest-growing medtech markets through 2030, margins should improve from manufacturing shifts, aligner profitability and operating leverage, and valuation sits below historical premiums. Catalysts are Q3 results on 28 Oct 2026 and China tender outcomes in Q4 2026.

Rolls-Royce (Buy | MP, PT GBP 19): UBS sees the turnaround as incomplete and expects further earnings upgrades. February 2027 results (FY26 around 23 Feb 2027) may bring higher medium-term cash flow guidance. Civil Aerospace margins are forecast to reach top-peer levels, Defence profitability to exceed most peers, and Power Systems benefits from data centre backup demand.

Siemens (Buy | MP, PT EUR 330): UBS expects a strong Q4 on 12 Nov with core orders growth led by Mobility and Smart Infrastructure. Digital Industries depends on an automation recovery and software improvement. FY27 guidance should support margin expansion as Altair and Dotmatics integration costs fade, and the Healthineers deconsolidation and buybacks may support the shares.

Barclays (Buy | MP, PT GBP 5.70): UBS cites investment banking momentum, structural hedging that supports earnings resilience, cost actions, capital returns and diversification across retail, cards and corporate banking. The bank sees the stock as undervalued versus peers.

ROCKWOOL (Buy, PT DKK 265): Q2 results showed strong volumes, pricing power and margins, and the shares fell over 10% on limited estimate changes, which UBS calls a better entry point. UBS is ahead of consensus for FY26 to FY28, July price increases are confirmed, and valuation is near the low end of its historical range.

Oracle (Buy | MP, PT USD 250): The PDF's Oracle page repeats the Boeing bullet text (about USD 750bn backlog, free cash flow rising from USD 2.2bn in 2026 to USD 15.1bn by 2030), which appears to be a copy error. The company profile says Oracle plans 10 GW of data center capacity by fiscal 2028 year-end. The valuation statement uses a FCF multiple and cites the 28 Oct 2026 note 'Creditors Applaud, Hence So Do We'.

Boeing (Buy | MP, PT USD 240): UBS cites a backlog of nearly USD 750bn, reset expectations with conservative guidance, free cash flow rising from USD 2.2bn in 2026 to USD 15.1bn by 2030, and recent defense wins. The PT reflects 20.5x EV/EBITDA, and the shares are 10.5% below inception and near the lower trade boundary of USD 163.81.

Expeditors (Buy, PT USD 245): Airfreight demand from data center and technology customers is described as exceptionally strong. AI tools and technology restructuring should lift productivity and margins, customs activity benefits from trade complexity, and UBS raised earnings forecasts after Q2.

Orica (Buy | MP, PT AUD 27): Resilient mine activity and tight ammonium nitrate markets support earnings, recent acquisitions and a cost reduction program help margins from 2027, and shares could re-rate if US ammonium nitrate supply concerns ease. Fiscal year 2026 results are due 12 November 2026.

Idea exit rules: each idea has absolute-return boundaries set by beta at inception (beta below 0.8: lower 9% / upper 12%; 0.8 to 1.2: 12% / 16%; above 1.2: 15% / 20%). Barclays at GBP 4.24 is above its lower level of 4.08, Boeing at 172.5 is above 163.81, and Oracle at 115.16 is above 101.34.

sector_views.rationale: Rolls-Royce and Boeing are both Buy | MP, citing earnings upgrades, civil aerospace recovery, defense wins and data centre backup power demand.
Barclays is a Buy | MP on investment banking revenue, structural hedging, cost actions and valuation versus peers.
Siemens is a Buy | MP on Smart Infrastructure and Mobility orders and FY27 margin expansion.
Straumann is a Buy on dental implant market growth, aligner profitability and valuation below historical premiums.
Oracle is a Buy | MP on data center capacity expansion.
Expeditors is a Buy on airfreight demand from data center and technology customers.
Orica is a Buy | MP on mining activity and ammonium nitrate pricing.
ROCKWOOL is a Buy after a 10%+ post-Q2 share price fall, with volumes and pricing ahead of consensus.

earnings_insights: Siemens Q4 results are due 12 Nov 2026. UBS expects strong core orders growth led by Mobility and Smart Infrastructure and says the Digital Industries FY27 margin guide will be key. This is a UBS expectation, not a printed result.
Orica fiscal year 2026 result is due 12 November 2026. UBS cites it as a catalyst. Not yet printed.
Straumann Q3 results were scheduled for 28 Oct 2026 and China tender outcomes for Q4 2026. The document does not state the Q3 outcome.
Rolls-Royce FY26 results are expected around 23 Feb 2027, with potential guidance upgrade and higher medium-term cash flow guidance (UBS expectation).
ROCKWOOL Q2 results showed strong volumes and pricing and the shares fell over 10% on limited estimate changes. UBS says it is ahead of consensus for FY26, FY27 and FY28 (no figures given).
Expeditors: UBS raised earnings forecasts following stronger Q2 execution and demand (no figures given).
Boeing: UBS forecasts free cash flow of USD 2.2bn in 2026 rising to USD 15.1bn by 2030. The valuation statement says Boeing has a 0% YTD adjusted EBIT margin after charges on development programs.

Siemens: cyclical end-markets and a history of exceptional charges that cut income below expectations.
Barclays: UK credit and rate exposure, capital markets volatility and regulatory change.
Straumann: dental implant market cyclicality, product launch issues, discount competition and FX.
